name: Aqara Hub M3 (EU)

radios.note: EU page lists dual-band Wi-Fi and a PoE Ethernet port; CSA's Zigbee listing mentions Thread and Bluetooth child devices. Model number HM-G01D comes from retailers only.

matter.note: CSA's Aqara Hub Platform software certificate lists Hub M3; a separate Hub M3 Matter certificate ID was seen in a CSA page but not opened. Transport shown as Wi-Fi; the hub also has Ethernet.

apple_home.note: Aqara lists Apple HomeKit. IR control is not supported through HomeKit.

smartthings.note: Aqara's developer docs list SmartThings among Matter bridge platforms.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's Works with program lists Aqara hubs including the M3, via Matter.

hubRequired.note: Not applicable to the hub itself; not assessed.

localControl.note: Aqara describes it as an edge hub with local automation storage; verifier should confirm wording.

deviceProtocols.note: Built-in 360 degree IR blaster; Bluetooth child devices per CSA listing.

matterBridge.note: Aqara's developer docs list it as a Matter bridge for Apple Home, Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings and Home Assistant. Some Aqara Zigbee devices cannot be exposed to Matter. Only one AC device can be exposed to Matter.

threadBorderRouter.note: Aqara's FAQ says the hub acts as a Thread Border Router.

maxDevices.note: Maker gives two figures: up to 127 Thread/Zigbee devices, but the FAQ says 64 direct child devices and 127 through routers or mesh extenders.

summary: Placeholder summary pending the editor: this record lists what the hub connects to and which ecosystems see those devices. Aqara Zigbee, Thread and Matter hub with an IR blaster, EU version.
